name: Baked Char Siu Bao
desc: Soft milk-bread buns baked around a sweet, saucy Chinese BBQ pork filling.

source.title: Chinese BBQ Pork Buns (Baked Char Siu Bao)
source.evidence: Every ingredient and amount matches the Woks of Life recipe card line for line, as does the method (15-minute knead, 75-90 minute proof, 16 buns, 400°F dropped to 350°F).

ingredients.raw: 2/3 cup heavy cream, at room temperature
1 cup whole milk, at room temperature
1/2 cup cake flour (or 1/2 cup all-purpose flour sifted with 1 tbsp cornstarch)
ingredients.note: or 1/2 cup all-purpose flour sifted with 1 tbsp cornstarch

ingredients.raw: 3 1/2 cups bread flour, plus more for dusting
1 tbsp active dry yeast (or instant yeast)
1/2 cup finely chopped shallots (or yellow onion)
2 cups finely diced Chinese roast pork (char siu)
1 large egg, beaten with 1 tbsp water (egg wash)
1 tbsp granulated sugar, dissolved in 1 tbsp boiling water (glaze)

steps: Make the dough: In the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the dough hook, add the dough ingredients in this order: heavy cream, milk, egg, sugar, cake flour, bread flour, yeast, and salt. Mix on the lowest speed until a scraggly dough forms, then knead on low for 15 minutes. The dough should stick to the bottom of the bowl but not the sides; if it sticks to the sides, add flour 1 tbsp at a time.
Shape the dough into a ball, cover with a damp towel or an overturned plate, and let it proof in a warm spot for 75-90 minutes, until doubled in size.

Make the filling while the dough proofs: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the shallots and stir-fry for 2 minutes. Add the sugar, light soy sauce, oyster sauce, sesame oil, and dark soy sauce and stir until it begins to bubble.

Add the chicken stock and flour, reduce the heat to medium-low, and cook, stirring, for 2-3 minutes until thickened. Stir in the diced pork. Spread the filling on a plate, divide it into 16 equal piles, and let it cool.
Knead the proofed dough for 5 minutes to knock out the air, then turn it onto a lightly floured surface and cut it into 16 equal pieces (weigh the dough and divide by 16 for even buns).

Knead each piece smooth and roll it into a 4-inch circle, slightly thicker in the center than at the edges. With clean, grease-free fingers, add one pile of filling, crimp the dough closed, and seal tightly.
Set the buns seam side down on 2 parchment-lined baking sheets, about 3 inches apart. Cover with a clean towel and let rise at room temperature for 1 hour.
Position racks in the top and bottom thirds of the oven and preheat to 400°F. Brush the buns with egg wash and sprinkle with sesame seeds, if using.
Put the buns in the oven and immediately lower the temperature to 350°F. Bake for 22-25 minutes, until golden brown.
Brush the hot buns with the sugar syrup as soon as they come out of the oven. Cool slightly before serving.
tips: The filling needs 2 cups of cooked char siu, which takes about 9 hours with its overnight marinade; make it a day ahead with the Char Siu recipe on this site.
No stand mixer: stir the dough together with a wooden spoon and knead by hand for 20 minutes.
